title: Reliability playback & ops sync brainstorm
content:
Purpose: quick prep notes for the weekly SRE ops sync — combine a short SLO snapshot, paging trend signals, short writeups for top incidents from last two weeks, and a lightweight set of proposed follow-ups we can triage live. This is a personal scratchpad; bring what looks useful to the sync.

Agenda (10–30m):
- 0–3m: Flash SLO snapshot + burn rate (Maya)
- 3–8m: Paging trends & emergent patterns (open mic)
- 8–18m: Top 3 incidents (auto-summaries + fast root-cause pointers)
- 18–25m: Quick wins & triage of follow-ups (owners, timelines)
- 25–30m: Any blockers for oncall fixes / rollouts

SLO snapshot (quick numbers — pull full dashboard before meeting):
- Uptime SLO (api.endpoints.global): target 99.95% monthly
  - Current month: 99.88% -> 0.07% breach so far (warning)
  - Error budget burn rate (7d): ~3.2x (elevated)
- Latency SLO (generation p99): target 800ms
  - Current p99 (24h): 920ms; p95 ~420ms
- Embeddings latency p95 target 200ms -> current 210ms (mild slip)

Paging trends (last 14 days):
- Pager volume: 28 total pages (compared to baseline 12)
  - Spike days: 3/29 and 4/02 (512 token workloads + cold cache)
  - Signal: majority are latency pages with correlated throttling messages from dedicated nodes
- Repeat callers: 4 teams generated 60% of paging noise (pricing-service + ingestion + A/B test infra)
- Time-of-day: most pages between 09:00–13:00 PT (traffic + cron jobs)

Top incidents (short recounts):
1) INC-2026-031-redis-cache-pressure
   - What: sudden KV cache growth from a background reindex job; caused mem pressure, evictions, longer KV lookups -> long tail generation latency, backpressure to router -> retries and downstream throttling pages.
   - Impact: ~45m of elevated p99s and several automatic failovers on dedicated pools.
   - Quick notes: reindex job ramping logic absent; cache TTLs defaulted to opt-in infinite.
   - Suspect root: unsafe reindex rollout + missing tenant-level rate limits
2) INC-2026-033-batch-scheduler-thundering
   - What: batch scheduler burst combined with small batching window misconfiguration; created CPU saturation on a subset of serving nodes causing request timeouts and queue growth.
   - Impact: ~30m timeouts for some customers on dedicated capacity; autoscaler failed to trigger in time for one pool.
   - Suspect root: spinner in batch window code path + autoscaler cooldown thresholds too conservative
3) INC-2026-039-degraded-tooling-telemetry
   - What: telemetry pipeline backlog dropped sampling; alert aggregation missed spikes -> delayed oncall response to a separate small outage.
   - Impact: delayed detection by ~10m; made mitigation slower.

Immediate remediation already done:
- Reindex job reverted to previous version (Anton)
- Cache TTLs patched to default 24h for unstable shards (hotfix)
- Emergency autoscaler cooldown override pushed to give headroom during bursts

Proposed follow-ups (triage items — assign during sync):
- F1 (high) — Add tenant-level rate limiter and safe ramp for reindex/replay jobs. Owner: Anton. ETA: 2026-04-20. Rationale: prevents single customer from evicting global cache.
- F2 (high) — Short-term: add guardrail alert when KV eviction rate > X and p99 > Y. Owner: Diego. ETA: 2026-04-10.
- F3 (medium) — Revisit autoscaler cooldown and aggressive burst detection rules for dedicated pools. Owner: SRE-Auto team (Rhea triage). ETA: 2026-04-15.
- F4 (medium) — Batching window audit: instrument distribution of batch sizes, expose per-model histograms. Owner: Serving Runtime (assign engineer). ETA: 2026-04-14.
- F5 (low) — Telemetry sampling: short spike-detection bypass to raise sample rate for alerts when noise increases. Owner: Observability infra. ETA: 2026-04-21.

Notes / questions to bring up in sync:
- Do we want a short-term SLO burn-mode playbook? If error budget > 2x burn we move to coordinated mitigations (e.g., lower noncritical batch priority, reduce background jobs).
- Consider temporary customer-level soft-throttles (graceful degradation) for noisy tenants — product/CS buy-in needed.
- Can we add a lightweight oncall-runbook checklist item: \"check telemetry ingest health\" before fighting symptoms? Would have flagged INC-2026-039 earlier.

Personal quick wins I can push this week (Maya):
- Draft a one-page runbook addendum for reindex jobs (safe ramp, throttles, required reviews) — will PR by 4/09.
- Prototype a simple eviction-rate alert in dev and roll to prod canaries — target 4/10.

Unresolved / followups I want to capture in meeting:
- Exact thresholds for eviction-rate alert (need historical baseline) — ask Diego for 60–90 day metrics.
- Who on Product owns tenant throttling policy (need contact before proposing enforcement).
- Whether dedicated autoscaler cooldown change needs capacity approval (finance/infra budget).

Meeting prep checklist (for me):
- Pull current SLO dashboard + 7d/30d trend graphs
- Slack pre-brief to Anton & Rhea with top 2 remediations
- Create short jira tickets for F1/F2 to quickly allocate in sync

Post-meeting expected outputs:
- 3 prioritized Jira tickets with owners and ETA
- Decision on whether to enter \"error-budget mitigation\" mode
- Runbook PR created or at least a draft link

Random brain dumps (keep for later) :
- Could we do per-tenant KV quotas using existing shard labels? Might be lightweight and stop noisy tenants before global impact.
- Evaluate a short-lived \"priority lane\" in the router for critical traffic to bypass large batch queues during high load.

Quick references:
- SLO dashboard (confluence): https://confluence.redwood/team/slo-dashboard
- Recent incidents log: https://confluence.redwood/incidents/2026-q2
- Pager thread: slack:#sre-oncall -> thread ts:1712000000.000100

End of scratchpad. Bring anything you think is urgent.

-- Maya
